chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abdul Rahman ibn Zayaba, who said:

A woman bequeathed to me, saying: 'From my third, pay off my debt, and a part of it is for So-and-so.' So I asked Ibn Abi Layla about that, and he said: 'I do not see anything for her, as I do not know what 'a part' is.' Then I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about it after that, and informed him how the woman had spoken and what Ibn Abi Layla had said. He said: 'Ibn Abi Layla has lied. For her is a tenth of the third. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ibrahim (peace be upon him), saying: 'Place on every mountain of them a part' — and the mountains at that time were ten, and 'a part' is the tenth of the thing.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal definition of 'a part' (juz') in Islamic inheritance and bequests according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the technical legal definition of 'part' (juz') as one-tenth (ushr) within the context of Islamic inheritance law, correcting the earlier jurist Ibn Abi Layla's uncertainty. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) grounds this interpretation in the Quranic narrative of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), where ten mountains were created, each receiving a 'part,' thereby linking linguistic precision to divine precedent. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on deriving specific legal quantifiers from Quranic exegesis to resolve ambiguities in bequests.
